rules.sentence: Although Sjögren syndrome can develop at any age, symptoms most commonly begin between the ages of 45 and 55.
The lack of an evidence-based, standardized screening tool to identify which dry eye patients require evaluation for Sjögren syndrome contributes to the underreferral of these individuals.
As a result, many cases of Sjögren syndrome remain undiagnosed, perpetuating a pattern of underrecognition and delayed diagnosis.[8]
Sjögren syndrome affects approximately 0.5% to 1.0% of the population, with an incidence approaching half that of rheumatoid arthritis.
Approximately half of those diagnosed also have rheumatoid arthritis or another connective tissue disease (eg, lupus).
